scope: Local single-sender release benchmark; actual DAVE, RTP and loopback UDP; 10 seconds after 1 second warmup. Not an Oracle or internet quality result.
interpretation: Both retained zero steady allocations and approximately 50 frames/s; latency differences in this one run are not claimed as a speedup.

regression.before: Failed instead of Stopped, no media frame delivered
regression.after: Stopped normally after sending the valid frame and silence drain; elapsed overrun still counted
regression.simulation: 20 ms thread sleep models wall time without CPU use; not a valid production source implementation

limits: This does not establish the cause of the earlier unclassified Oracle terminal failure.
Linux only: sleeping or blocking callbacks still violate the source contract but are not detected by the CPU-time guard.
No claim of reduced internet jitter or CPU usage from the one local benchmark pair.

activeDelayRegression.before: A 30 ms off-CPU delay in active playback produced catch-up polling less than 15 ms after the delayed frame.
activeDelayRegression.after: After an entire missed period during poll/encrypt/send, retain the valid frame, reset the absolute pacing deadline to completion + 20 ms, and discard the capacity-one old deadline.
activeDelayRegression.scope: Tests resumed delivery and no catch-up; does not make shared-host delays disappear.
